docs.title: VFA — Visual & Functional Web Auditor
docs.text:
VFA is an autonomous black-box web QA agent. It navigates real browsers, reasons about what it sees, and reports functional defects, console errors and broken network calls — without access to your source code, test IDs or internal APIs.

VFA ships as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over stdio. Any MCP-capable client (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Roo Code, Cline, custom agents) can hand it a URL or a natural-language user flow and receive a structured, machine-readable audit report back.

# Zero-docker, zero-infrastructure: one command to run the server
uvx vfa-mcp

Commercial license required

VFA is a commercial product distributed through Creem. A single-seat VFA_LICENSE_KEY is required to start the server. See Quickstart & License for activation details.

docs.title: Key pillars
docs.text: Pillar What it means in practice Native Zero-Docker Uses a locally installed Playwright Chromium — no containers, no remote browser farms, no extra services to operate. VFA runs wherever your MCP client runs, including locked-down corporate laptops. Universal LiteLLM Engine The reasoning layer is provider-agnostic through LiteLLM. DeepSeek, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Azure, or a local Ollama instance — switch with one environment variable, no code changes. Active Visual Grounding VFA does not rely on brittle CSS/XPath selectors. It screenshots the live page, maps the DOM into an annotated snapshot, and grounds element interactions in what a human would actually see. 1-Click Execution uvx vfa-mcp bootstraps the server with no clone, no virtualenv and no build step. PyPI distribution plus an ephemeral dependency cache keeps startup under a few seconds.

docs.title: Architecture at a glance
docs.text:
┌──────────────────┐   stdio (JSON-RPC)   ┌──────────────────────────┐
│  MCP Client      │ ◄──────────────────► │  VFA MCP Server          │
│  (Cursor, Claude │                      │  ├─ License gate (Creem) │
│   Desktop, ...)  │                      │  ├─ Tool router          │
└──────────────────┘                      │  ├─ LLM engine (LiteLLM) │
                                          │  └─ Browser orchestrator │
                                          └───────────┬──────────────┘
                                                      │ CDP
                                          ┌───────────▼──────────────┐
                                          │ Playwright Chromium      │
                                          │ (ephemeral contexts)     │
                                          └──────────────────────────┘

Every invocation spawns a short-lived BrowserContext, performs the audit, drains the telemetry buffer and tears the context down. Nothing is persisted between runs unless you explicitly enable the session pool.

docs.title: Security overview
docs.text:
Black-box auditing means pointing an autonomous agent at live web pages — VFA treats that as a hostile environment by default.

Control Description Ephemeral BrowserContext Each audit runs in a fresh, isolated context with its own cookie jar, cache and storage. Contexts are destroyed at end of run, so credentials and session state never leak across audits or tenants. Anti-SSRF firewall Outbound navigation targets are resolved and validated before the browser is allowed to connect. Loopback, link-local, and private address ranges are blocked unless VFA_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOST=true is explicitly set for local testing. Strict Chromium isolation Chromium runs with a hardened flag set, restricted permissions, and no access to the host filesystem, clipboard or microphone/camera endpoints. Downloads and file pickers are denied by policy. Least-privilege tooling Tools accept URLs and natural-language steps only. There is no arbitrary JavaScript evaluation endpoint and no shell execution surface exposed to the LLM.

Local network testing

Setting VFA_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOST=true disables the anti-SSRF guard for loopback and private ranges. Only enable it on trusted machines. See Environment Variables for the full reference.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
VFA is configured exclusively through environment variables. In MCP clients they are declared in the env block of the server definition; for standalone runs they are plain shell exports.

Precedence

A variable defined in the MCP client's env block always wins over the parent shell environment, which in turn wins over VFA's built-in defaults.

docs.title: Core settings
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description VFA_LICENSE_KEY Yes — Creem single-seat license key. Validated at startup and refreshed periodically; an invalid or over-activated key aborts the server with LICENSE_INVALID. VFA_LLM_PROVIDER Yes — LiteLLM provider prefix used for the reasoning model (deepseek, anthropic, gemini, openrouter, ollama, azure, …). VFA_LLM_MODEL Yes — Model identifier passed to the provider, e.g. deepseek-chat, claude-3-5-sonnet-latest, gemini-2.0-flash-exp. VFA_LLM_API_KEY Yes* — API key for the reasoning provider. VFA_LLM_BASE_URL No Provider default Overrides the provider endpoint. Required for self-hosted gateways, proxies, Azure deployments and local Ollama.

* Not needed when the target provider requires no authentication (a local Ollama daemon, for example).

docs.title: Vision overrides
docs.text:
The vision model performs screenshot understanding and visual grounding. When any VFA_VISION_* variable is set, the vision sub-system stops inheriting the core LLM settings and uses the dedicated model instead — useful for pairing a cheap text model with a strong vision model.

Variable Required Default Description VFA_VISION_PROVIDER No Value of VFA_LLM_PROVIDER LiteLLM provider used for screenshot analysis and visual grounding. VFA_VISION_MODEL No Value of VFA_LLM_MODEL Vision-capable model identifier. Must accept image inputs. VFA_VISION_API_KEY No Value of VFA_LLM_API_KEY API key for the vision provider, when it differs from the text provider.

Vision-capable models only

Setting VFA_VISION_MODEL to a text-only model (for example deepseek-chat) causes grounding to degrade to DOM heuristics and can fail audits that depend on visual confirmation. Use a multimodal model.

docs.title: Runtime & browser
docs.text:
Variable Required Default Description HEADLESS No true Runs Chromium without a visible window. Set to false to watch the audit live while debugging. VFA_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOST No false Disables the anti-SSRF firewall so VFA can reach localhost and private ranges. Enable only for trusted local testing. BROWSER_CDP_URL No — Connects to an existing Chromium over CDP instead of launching a managed browser, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9222. Useful for reusing an authenticated session. VFA_SESSION_POOL_ENABLED No false Keeps warmed browser contexts alive between audits to cut cold-start latency. Contexts remain isolated per run; disable on shared or multi-tenant machines.

Anti-SSRF bypass

VFA_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOST=true lets the agent navigate to cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) and internal services. Never enable it inside an environment that shares a network with production infrastructure.

docs.title: Drop-in presets
docs.text:
Copy the block for your provider into the env object of your MCP client configuration, or export it in your shell.

Placeholder credentials

Every key below is a documentation placeholder of the form YOUR_*_API_KEY — none of them is a real credential or a valid key format. Substitute your own values and keep them out of version control.

DeepSeekClaude 3.5 SonnetGemini 2.0 FlashOpenRouterLocal Ollama 
export VFA_LLM_PROVIDER="deepseek"
export VFA_LLM_MODEL="deepseek-chat"
export VFA_LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"
export VFA_LLM_BASE_URL="https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
# DeepSeek is text-only: pair it with a vision model for grounding
export VFA_VISION_PROVIDER="gemini"
export VFA_VISION_MODEL="gemini-2.0-flash-exp"
export VFA_VISION_API_KEY="YOUR_GOOGLE_AI_STUDIO_KEY"

The lowest-cost configuration. Because deepseek-chat has no vision support, a vision override is strongly recommended.

export VFA_LLM_PROVIDER="anthropic"
export VFA_LLM_MODEL="claude-3-5-sonnet-latest"
export VFA_LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
# No vision override needed: the core model is multimodal

The reference configuration — best grounding quality for complex flows. One model handles both reasoning and vision, so no override is necessary.

export VFA_LLM_PROVIDER="gemini"
export VFA_LLM_MODEL="gemini-2.0-flash-exp"
export VFA_LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_GOOGLE_AI_STUDIO_KEY"

Fast, cheap and multimodal — a balanced default for high-volume audit runs.

export VFA_LLM_PROVIDER="openrouter"
export VFA_LLM_MODEL="anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet"
export VFA_LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
export VFA_LLM_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
# Route screenshots to a cheaper multimodal model while keeping Sonnet for reasoning
export VFA_VISION_PROVIDER="openrouter"
export VFA_VISION_MODEL="google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free"

Any model available on OpenRouter can be selected by changing VFA_LLM_MODEL — the provider prefix in the model string follows OpenRouter's own namespace.

export VFA_LLM_PROVIDER="ollama"
export VFA_LLM_MODEL="llama3.1:70b"
export VFA_LLM_BASE_URL="http://localhost:11434"
# VFA_LLM_API_KEY is not required for a local daemon
export VFA_VISION_PROVIDER="ollama"
export VFA_VISION_MODEL="llava:latest"
# Chrome does not need to reach a private range, but the model does:
# keep the anti-SSRF guard on unless you are auditing local apps
export VFA_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOST="false"

Fully offline reasoning. VFA_LICENSE_KEY still requires one activation call to Creem; after the license is cached, subsequent runs work without internet access.

docs.title: Validation checklist
docs.text:
Before opening an issue, confirm the following:

  1. VFA_LICENSE_KEY is present in the client's env block, not only in your shell.
  2. VFA_LLM_MODEL exists for the chosen VFA_LLM_PROVIDER (a mismatch surfaces as a provider 404 model_not_found error).
  3. playwright install chromium has been executed for the same Python interpreter that runs VFA.
  4. Any VFA_VISION_MODEL you set accepts image inputs.

docs.title: Quickstart & License
docs.text: Get VFA running inside your MCP client in under five minutes.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
Requirement Notes Python 3.10+ Only needed for the pip install path. uvx manages its own runtime. uv / uvx Recommended launcher. Install with curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh. Playwright Chromium VFA drives a local browser. Install the binary once with the command below. LLM API key Any provider supported by LiteLLM (DeepSeek, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, Ollama…). Creem license A single-seat VFA_LICENSE_KEY — required, the server refuses to start without it. 
# Install the Chromium build Playwright needs (run once per machine)
playwright install chromium

If playwright is not on your PATH, use python -m playwright install chromium, or let uvx do it: uvx --from playwright playwright install chromium.

docs.title: 2. Activate your license
docs.text:
VFA is sold and licensed through Creem. After purchase, your Creem receipt contains a license key in the VFA- prefixed format; copy it from the customer portal. The key is validated at server startup and refreshed periodically during the session.

export VFA_LICENSE_KEY="YOUR_CREEM_LICENSE_KEY"

Single-seat license

A license is bound to one seat. Sharing a key across machines or running concurrent instances under the same key will trigger Creem's activation limit and the server will exit with a LICENSE_INVALID error. Deactivate old machines from your Creem customer portal before moving to a new one.

Never hardcode the key in a commit

Store VFA_LICENSE_KEY in your shell profile, a secret manager, or the env block of your MCP client configuration — never in a tracked file.

docs.title: 3. Configure your LLM provider
docs.text:
At minimum, set a provider, a model and an API key:

export VFA_LLM_PROVIDER="deepseek"
export VFA_LLM_MODEL="deepseek-chat"
export VFA_LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_PROVIDER_API_KEY"

Check Environment Variables for the complete reference and copy-paste presets per provider.

docs.title: 4. Wire VFA into your MCP client
docs.text:
Every snippet below injects VFA_LICENSE_KEY (plus your LLM credentials) into the server's env block.

Placeholder credentials

Values such as YOUR_CREEM_LICENSE_KEY and YOUR_PROVIDER_API_KEY are documentation placeholders, not valid credentials. Replace them with your own Creem license and provider key before saving the file.

CursorClaude DesktopRoo Code / Cline

Create or edit .cursor/mcp.json (project-scoped) or ~/.cursor/mcp.json (global):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vfa": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["vfa-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "VFA_LICENSE_KEY": "YOUR_CREEM_LICENSE_KEY",
        "VFA_LLM_PROVIDER": "deepseek",
        "VFA_LLM_MODEL": "deepseek-chat",
        "VFA_LLM_API_KEY": "YOUR_PROVIDER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}

Reload the window, then confirm vfa appears as a connected server under Settings → MCP.

Edit claude_desktop_config.json:

  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
  • Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vfa": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["vfa-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "VFA_LICENSE_KEY": "YOUR_CREEM_LICENSE_KEY",
        "VFA_LLM_PROVIDER": "anthropic",
        "VFA_LLM_MODEL": "claude-3-5-sonnet-latest",
        "VFA_LLM_API_KEY": "YOUR_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}

Quit Claude Desktop completely (tray icon → Quit) and reopen it. Tools are discovered on startup.

Edit the extension's mcpSettings.json (MCP Servers → Edit MCP Settings):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vfa": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["vfa-mcp"],
      "disabled": false,
      "autoApprove": [],
      "env": {
        "VFA_LICENSE_KEY": "YOUR_CREEM_LICENSE_KEY",
        "VFA_LLM_PROVIDER": "openrouter",
        "VFA_LLM_MODEL": "anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet",
        "VFA_LLM_API_KEY": "YOUR_OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}

Roo Code and Cline both read the same settings file format; keep autoApprove empty so every audit requires explicit confirmation.

Windows paths

On Windows, quote the command if it contains spaces, e.g. "command": "C:\\Users\\you\\.local\\bin\\uvx.exe". Run where uvx to find the exact path.

docs.title: 5. Verify the installation
docs.text:
Ask your client to audit a public URL:

Use qa_audit_url to audit https://example.com and summarize the findings.

A healthy response returns a JSON report containing status, findings, screenshots and metrics. If the server fails to appear, check the client's MCP log output — the usual causes are a missing VFA_LICENSE_KEY, an expired key, or Chromium not being installed.

docs.title: Standalone CLI execution
docs.text:
VFA is also runnable without any client integration, which is handy for CI pipelines or debugging:

pip install vfa-mcp
playwright install chromium
export VFA_LICENSE_KEY="YOUR_CREEM_LICENSE_KEY"

vfa-mcp --help

The process speaks JSON-RPC over stdio, exactly like the client-managed launch — pipe a tools/call request into it and read the response from stdout.

docs.text:
• Environment Variables — every knob, plus provider presets.
  • MCP Tools — parameter contracts and output schemas.

docs.title: MCP Tools
docs.text:
VFA exposes three tools over stdio. All of them return a single JSON object; failures return a structured error object instead of raising, so an agent can reason about them.

Tool Purpose qa_audit_url Autonomous black-box audit of a single page. qa_execute_user_flow Drives a multi-step natural-language user journey. qa_get_runtime_errors Drains the buffered runtime error channel.

Every invocation runs inside an isolated, ephemeral BrowserContext that is destroyed on completion. See the security overview for the guarantees this provides.

docs.title: qa_audit_url
docs.text: Opens a URL, waits for network idle, inspects the rendered page and reports functional, visual and accessibility defects together with any console or network errors collected during the visit.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Default Description url string Yes — Absolute http/https URL to audit. Private and loopback targets are rejected unless VFA_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOST=true. viewport object No {"width": 1440, "height": 900} Viewport used for rendering and screenshots. wait_until string No "networkidle" Load strategy: load, domcontentloaded or networkidle. max_depth integer No 1 Follow same-origin links up to this depth. 0 audits only the entry page. include_screenshots boolean No true Attach base64 screenshots (viewport and full page) to the report. focus string No — Free-text hint narrowing the audit, e.g. "checkout funnel and form validation".

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Validates the target against the anti-SSRF firewall and the license gate.
  2. Creates a fresh context, navigates and waits for the requested load state.
  3. Captures a full-page screenshot and an annotated DOM snapshot for visual grounding.
  4. Runs the reasoning pass: broken layouts, unreachable controls, missing labels, console errors and HTTP failures >= 400 are all correlated into findings.
  5. Returns the report and tears the context down.

docs.title: Output schema
docs.text:
{
  "status": "completed",
  "url": "https://example.com/pricing",
  "duration_ms": 41230,
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "FND-001",
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "functional",
      "title": "Primary CTA does not respond to click",
      "description": "Clicking 'Start free trial' produces no navigation and no state change.",
      "selector_hint": "button[data-testid='trial-cta']",
      "evidence": {
        "screenshot_index": 0,
        "console_errors": 1
      }
    }
  ],
  "metrics": {
    "pages_audited": 3,
    "console_errors": 2,
    "http_errors": 1,
    "duration_ms": 41230
  },
  "screenshots": [
    { "name": "viewport", "mime_type": "image/png", "data": "<base64>" }
  ]
}

severity is one of critical, high, medium, low, info. category is one of functional, visual, accessibility, performance, network.

docs.title: qa_execute_user_flow
docs.text: Executes a defined user journey — written in natural language — against a starting URL. This is the functional counterpart to qa_audit_url: instead of inspecting a single page, VFA attempts to complete a task the way a real user would, and reports where it got stuck.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Default Description url string Yes — Entry point of the flow. Must be an absolute http/https URL. steps array Yes — Ordered list of natural-language steps. Minimum length is 1. expected_outcome string No — Natural-language success condition, e.g. "the order confirmation page is shown". timeout_ms integer No 120000 Total budget for the whole flow. stop_on_failure boolean No true Abort on the first failed step instead of continuing optimistically.

docs.title: Step format
docs.text:
Each entry in steps is a plain string describing intent, not a selector:

{
  "url": "https://shop.example.com",
  "steps": [
    "Open the product page for the first item in the catalog",
    "Select size M and add the item to the cart",
    "Go to the cart and apply the coupon code SAVE10",
    "Proceed to checkout without creating an account",
    "Fill the shipping form with a test address and submit"
  ],
  "expected_outcome": "The order confirmation page displays an order number",
  "timeout_ms": 180000
}

VFA resolves each step through active visual grounding: the screenshot and annotated DOM are analyzed to locate the element a human would interact with, then the action is replayed in the browser. Failed steps include the reason and the last observed page state.

docs.title: Output schema
docs.text:
{
  "status": "failed",
  "url": "https://shop.example.com",
  "expected_outcome": "The order confirmation page displays an order number",
  "steps": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "instruction": "Open the product page for the first item in the catalog",
      "status": "success",
      "action": "click",
      "target": "a.product-card__link",
      "duration_ms": 3120
    },
    {
      "index": 2,
      "instruction": "Go to the cart and apply the coupon code SAVE10",
      "status": "failed",
      "action": "fill",
      "target": "input[name='coupon']",
      "error": "Coupon field present but the apply button stayed disabled after input.",
      "duration_ms": 18400
    }
  ],
  "outcome_matched": false,
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "FND-014",
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "functional",
      "title": "Coupon apply button never enables",
      "description": "The apply button is disabled even with a syntactically valid coupon code."
    }
  ],
  "metrics": {
    "steps_total": 5,
    "steps_succeeded": 2,
    "steps_failed": 1,
    "steps_skipped": 2,
    "duration_ms": 60510
  },
  "screenshots": [
    { "name": "step_2_failure", "mime_type": "image/png", "data": "<base64>" }
  ]
}

status is completed, failed or timeout. A steps[].status of skipped appears when stop_on_failure is true and an earlier step already failed.

docs.title: qa_get_runtime_errors
docs.text: Drains VFA's runtime error buffer. The buffer collects everything the browser reported while auditing, independent of what the reasoning model decided to report as findings — useful when an agent wants raw evidence or a post-run regression signal.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Required Default Description clear boolean No true Empties the buffer after reading. Set to false to peek without draining. source string No "all" Filter by origin: console, pageerror, http or all. min_severity string No "info" Drop entries below this level (info, warning, error).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The buffer is populated continuously during every audit and flow run. It captures three channels:

  • console — console.warn, console.error and uncaught assertions emitted by the page.
  • pageerror — uncaught JavaScript exceptions, including stack traces.
  • http — every response with status >= 400, with method, URL and response time.

Calling the tool with clear: true returns the entries and empties the buffer, which keeps successive agent turns from re-reading the same events.

docs.title: Output schema
docs.text:
{
  "status": "completed",
  "count": 3,
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "ERR-0001",
      "source": "console",
      "severity": "error",
      "level": "error",
      "message": "Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value')",
      "url": "https://shop.example.com/cart",
      "timestamp": "2025-01-14T10:22:41.512Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "ERR-0002",
      "source": "pageerror",
      "severity": "error",
      "message": "TypeError: cart.total is undefined",
      "stack": "at renderCart (cart.js:84:17)\n at HTMLDocument.dispatch (app.js:31:9)",
      "url": "https://shop.example.com/cart",
      "timestamp": "2025-01-14T10:22:41.517Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "ERR-0003",
      "source": "http",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "POST https://shop.example.com/api/coupon responded with 422",
      "status_code": 422,
      "duration_ms": 312,
      "url": "https://shop.example.com/cart",
      "timestamp": "2025-01-14T10:22:44.980Z"
    }
  ]
}

count reflects the number of entries returned in this call, not the historical total.

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
All three tools share a common failure shape:

{
  "status": "error",
  "error": {
    "code": "SSRF_BLOCKED",
    "message": "Target resolves to a private address; navigation refused.",
    "hint": "Set VFA_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOST=true to audit local applications."
  }
}
Code Meaning LICENSE_INVALID VFA_LICENSE_KEY missing, expired or activated on too many seats. SSRF_BLOCKED Target resolved to loopback, link-local or private space. NAVIGATION_FAILED DNS failure, TLS error or the page never reached the requested load state. LLM_PROVIDER_ERROR Upstream provider rejected the request (bad key, unknown model, rate limit). BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE Chromium binary missing — run playwright install chromium. TIMEOUT The audit exceeded timeout_ms.

See Environment Variables for the settings referenced above.
